I am a quantitative social science researcher with interests in using data science techniques to create data informed policy recommendations. I am open to pursuing applied research opportunities studying immigration, housing, urban planning, polarization, or public opinion in Canada or other advanced democracies. I have previously contributed to the Canadian Election Study ([CES](http://www.ces-eec.ca)) and worked extensively as a research assistant for the Laurier Institute for the Study of Public Opinion and Policy ([LISPOP](https://lispop.ca)), [Dr. Aaron Erlich](https://www.aaronerlich.com/demotip-laboratory) and [Dr. Dietlind Stolle](https://www.mcgill.ca/politicalscience/dietlind-stolle).

I am currently completing my Masters degree in the political science department at [McGill University](https://www.mcgill.ca/politicalscience/) and the Centre for the Study of Democratic Citizenship ([CSDC](https://csdc-cecd.ca/members/students/?studentid=547)). My research is in the sub-fields on **comparative** and **Canadian politics** and focuses on the causes and consequences of political polarization and quantitative methodology. My current research is supported by the *Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada* and the *Fonds de recherche du Québec - Société et culture (FRQ-SC)*.

I previously revived a Bachelor's degree in Political Science from [Wilfrid Laurier University](https://students.wlu.ca/programs/arts/political-science/index.html).
